text:
riley: Hey folks, first-day question. Trying to get devbox ready on an M2 Mac and a WSL Ubuntu VM. Installed brew + asdf, pulled the repo, but running into a couple weird things:
- asdf/nodejs refuses to install Node (gpg signature errors)
- Ruby gems fail linking to OpenSSL during bundle install
- repo scripts expect REDWOOD_API_KEY and a kube context but I'm not sure the local pattern
Any quick checklist or who-to-ping?

samir: welcome! quick pointers: short TL;DR: asdf + direnv + rustup + proper openssl flags. Details: 1) Node/GPG: the asdf-nodejs plugin downloads Node releases signed by Node.js release team. install gnupg and run `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` (or follow plugin README) so gpg verification works. On mac: `brew install gnupg`.

2) OpenSSL / Ruby: on Apple silicon make sure `openssl@3` is installed via brew and set flags before `asdf install ruby` or `gem install`. Example: `export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"` and `export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"` and `export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib/pkgconfig"`. Then re-run `asdf install ruby` or reinstall the gems.

3) NVM vs asdf: avoid mixing nvm and asdf node shims. If you used nvm earlier, remove leftover lines from your shell rc or ensure asdf appears first in PATH. `asdf reshim nodejs` after install helps.

4) Native modules & Rust: if builds fail mentioning cargo, install rustup: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh` and add `~/.cargo/bin` to PATH. Some packages also require `python3` for node-gyp.

5) Kube + secrets: do NOT commit keys. We prefer direnv + a local config file. Create `~/.config/redwood/env.local` (gitignored) with `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-local-xxxx` and `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config-redwood`. Then in your repo `.envrc` add `source_env ~/.config/redwood/env.local`. If you need vault-backed creds or sops, ping dev-setup.

riley: thanks — where's the canonical dotfiles snippet? I saw a couple repos but not sure which is the "starter" one. Also the asdf node import script errored for me with a timeout.

dev-setup: we have a lightweight starter at https://github.com/redwood/devbox-dotfiles (copy-only pattern). It includes asdf init, direnv, sample `.envrc`, and `brew` packages we recommend. If the GPG import times out, try again with `GPG_TTY=$(tty)` and ensure your network allows github downloads; occasionally CI keys rotate and the import URL moves — fallback is to import keys manually from the Node release team keyring listed in the plugin README.

riley: got it. one last Q: kubeconfig — do I merge with my existing `~/.kube/config` or always use a separate file?

samir: either works. We prefer per-context files for safety: keep the prod kube out of your default kube config. Put provider files under `~/.kube/` and set `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config-redwood` in your env.local. If you need merging instructions, run `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/config-redwood kubectl config view --raw > ~/.kube/config.merged` then `mv ~/.kube/config.merged ~/.kube/config` after verifying.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-5183 for riley to get repo access and a dev kubecontext.

riley: awesome, i'll try those fixes (gnupg import, openssl flags, rustup) and post logs here if anything still breaks. thanks! :rocket:
